reason: This passage (Exodus 3) demonstrates Yahweh's explicit compassion and protective care for the Hebrew people. God states: 'I have surely seen the affliction of my people in Egypt and have heard their cries' (רָאֹה רָאִיתִי אֶת־ עֳנִי עַמִּי), indicates intimate knowledge of their suffering (יָדַעְתִּי אֶת־ מַכְאֹבָֽיו), and declares 'I have come down to deliver him' (וָאֵרֵד לְהַצִּיל֣וֹ). God promises to lead them to a good and spacious land and to provide favor in the sight of the Egyptians. The antagonism shown is exclusively toward Egypt's oppressors, not the Hebrew people themselves. The narrative presents Yahweh as actively rescuing and blessing the Hebrew people, which is the antithesis of antagonism.
